articles.title: Man posed as NFL player for San Francisco 49ers to defraud 26 women of $1.3 million, allegedly using dating apps, luxury cars and bogus investment accounts; FBI probes 61 potential victims
articles.summary: A man accused of posing as a San Francisco 49ers player allegedly used dating apps, luxury cars, a convincing social media presence and fake investment
articles.body: A man accused of posing as a San Francisco 49ers player allegedly used dating apps, luxury cars, a convincing social media presence and fake investment accounts to gain women’s trust and defraud them of approximately $1.3 million. Federal prosecutors allege that Daejon Labrayae Love, 35, and his alleged accomplice, Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, received the money from at least 26 women as part of a scheme involving fictitious investments.Love has pleaded not guilty to a federal felony charge of conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Meanwhile, the FBI is investigating claims from 35 additional women who have come forward, potentially taking the number of victims to 61. Their allegations are still being verified.According to the US Department of Justice (DOJ), the alleged scheme began in February 2022 and continued until the pair’s arrests on August 24, 2026. Love allegedly presented himself as a professional football player or wealthy real estate investor, while Chan allegedly posed as his financial adviser to convince women that the investments were legitimate.Woman grows suspicious after matching with alleged scammer on HingeDomonique DuBose, who matched with Love on the dating app Hinge, said she became suspicious when he allegedly claimed to be a professional football player. Speaking on The CyberGuy Report podcast, she explained to Fox News how she began investigating his claims rather than relying on his online profile.“Basically, I caught on right away,” DuBose said.Love’s Instagram account reportedly had around 85,000 followers and a blue verification checkmark. His posts featured San Francisco 49ers clothing, expensive cars and football-related imagery, including videos associated with the Super Bowl in New Orleans.“It looked valid. I mean, he had 85,000 followers. He had a blue check,” DuBose recalled.Despite the seemingly credible profile, she continued looking for evidence that Love had actually played for the team. She contacted a friend who had played for the 49ers, who initially believed Love’s claims were plausible. DuBose also checked the team’s roster, injured reserve list and practice squad, as well as his purported college football background.Another detail made her question the account: nearly every photograph appeared to feature 49ers merchandise. According to the report, federal investigators subsequently confirmed with representatives of the NFL and the 49ers that Love had never been employed by either organisation.Alleged scammer reportedly rushed to get her phone numberDuBose said Love’s advances felt unusually rapid after they connected on Hinge. Instead of sharing her personal number, she gave him her work phone number.“It was really fast how he wanted to get my number,” she told Fox News.She said Love began sending videos and voice recordings almost immediately, while making extravagant claims about his wealth and expressing a desire to spend time with her. One recording played during the podcast interview began, “So what’s up, beautiful? I had to shoot my shot with you.”“And it was just so fast. It was so rapid,” DuBose said, describing the frequency of his messages.She also recalled claims that Love came from a wealthy Swiss family and had ownership interests involving Gucci stores. The claims raised further questions for her about his purported career as a professional football player.Prosecutors allege Love used multiple identities and fake investment accountsAccording to court documents cited by the DOJ, Love allegedly used several names, including Jon Love, Daejon Love, Avril Lyto Love and Jordan Love, while presenting different professional backgrounds to people he encountered.He allegedly convinced women that they were in genuine romantic relationships with him and told some that he wanted to build wealth and a future together. Prosecutors say he portrayed himself as a sophisticated investor with a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars and promoted fictitious investment opportunities promising substantial returns.Chan allegedly reinforced those claims by posing as Love’s financial adviser. The pair reportedly exchanged electronic messages about supposed investment opportunities, which Love then shared with women to persuade them to transfer money.They also allegedly hosted three-way FaceTime calls during which they displayed fabricated investment gains. Love reportedly used phone applications to create fictitious bank and investment accounts showing large balances, presenting them as evidence of his wealth and the legitimacy of the investments.Women allegedly encouraged to take out personal loansAccording to the DOJ, Love and Chan solicited money through false representations about how the investments would work and the returns they could generate. Some women who did not have enough money to invest were allegedly encouraged to take out personal loans, with promises that they would be repaid quickly.DuBose said some women appeared to receive early investment returns, which encouraged them to invest more. However, federal investigators said none of the victims they interviewed reported receiving actual returns on their principal after sending money to Love and Chan. They also reportedly received no investment account information.Prosecutors allege that Love cut off communication when women ran out of money or began asking too many questions, while retaining the money they had sent.Financial records cited by investigators indicate that Love and Chan received approximately $1.3 million from the women. The alleged victims were based in Oregon, Washington, Idaho and California, according to the DOJ.Love pleads not guilty; judge orders him detainedLove pleaded not guilty on Tuesday to a felony charge of conspiracy to commit wire fraud. A public defender representing him did not respond to a request for comment, according to Fox News.Magistrate Judge Jolie A. Russo ordered Love detained, citing flight risk.The DOJ said arrest warrants and a criminal complaint against Love and Chan were issued on August 17, 2026, in the District of Oregon. On August 24, Chan allegedly flew from California to meet Love in Boise, Idaho, where the FBI and other law enforcement agencies apprehended both men at Boise Airport.Investigators reportedly learned that Love was in Idaho to meet new potential victims. The investigation also found that he had travelled to New Mexico, California, Oregon, Nevada, Utah and Idaho between July 15 and August 24, 2026.Both men were reported to be in federal custody in Boise following their arrests. The case is being investigated by the FBI and prosecuted by Assistant US Attorneys Bryan Chinwuba and Chris Cardani for the District of Oregon.FBI says 35 additional women have come forwardThe investigation expanded after the FBI reported on September 18 that 35 additional women had come forward with allegations that they had been defrauded. Investigators were still working to verify their claims. If confirmed, the number of identified victims could rise from 26 to 61.DuBose said some women described relationships with Love that had continued for years.“There’s some that dated him for 11, 12, 13 years off and on,” she said.She expressed distress over the alleged exploitation of women’s trust and emotions. “It breaks my heart,” she said, adding that she wanted to confront Love about his alleged actions. “I want to know why.”The FBI has urged anyone with information about Love or Chan to contact the agency through tips.fbi.gov or by calling 1-800-CALL-FBI.Dating app users urged to verify identities independentlyDuBose questioned how effectively dating platforms can prevent people from inventing identities.“As far as the dating apps go, you can be whoever you want on those dating apps. And that’s the scary part,” she said.She also described checking phone numbers and attempting to verify the identities of people she meets online.“If you text me the moment you text me, I’m reverse checking your number. I’m making sure your name is valid,” she said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, on Thursday strongly pushed back against Indian-origin Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal's social
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, on Thursday strongly pushed back against Indian-origin Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal's social media post on the country's democratic framework and electoral procedures, calling it an "interference" in India's internal affairs."The remarks by @RepJayapal on India’s electoral and political processes are unacceptable interference in India’s internal affairs," he posted on X.Emphasising India’s longstanding record of conducting free and fair elections, Kwatra invited Jayapal for a “constructive conversation” to address her concerns."India is a vibrant democracy, with robust, independent constitutional institutions and a longstanding record of free and fair elections. Always open to constructive conversation with the Congresswoman to dispel her misconceptions," he added.Kwatra's response came after Jayapal alleged a sweeping removal of citizens from India's draft electoral list."I am deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls. This appears to be a similar playbook to what the Trump Administration is doing here at home to undermine voting rights in a democracy," the Congresswoman said."Protecting democracies everywhere is essential work, and the Indian people — like the American people — deserve free and fair elections. Non-violent resistance movements are essential in these moments and I stand with the Indian people who are engaging in non-violent protests to counter anti-democratic efforts in India," she wrote in a follow-up post.Her remarks came amid the ongoing protests in India against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls exercise.According to data released by the Election Commission (EC), approximately 72 million entries were removed from draft electoral rolls across 13 states and Union territories during the initial two phases of the SIR.Furthermore, during the ongoing third phase, which encompasses the publication of draft lists across 18 states and UTs, the number of excluded electors totals 61.6 million.Addressing these omissions, the EC clarified that if a legitimate elector's name was accidentally omitted during the SIR process, the individual retains the right to apply for reinstatement through the claims and objections mechanism, followed by the submission of Form 6.(With ANI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Andhra Pradesh shocker: Lover lured to pond, beaten to death; husband, wife arrested
articles.summary: ELURU: Police have arrested a husband and wife accused of masterminding the murder of Thumula Lakshmana, 37, under Bhimadolu police station limits.
articles.body: ELURU: Police have arrested a husband and wife accused of masterminding the murder of Thumula Lakshmana, 37, under Bhimadolu police station limits. Bhimadolu Circle Inspector P. Krishna arrested Mamidi Gouri Shankar and his wife, Mamidi Lakshmi Durga, on Thursday.According to the police investigation, Lakshmana, a native of Ramabhadrapuram village in Vizianagaram district, had allegedly been in an extramarital relationship with Lakshmi Durga, who hailed from the same village. Disputes reportedly arose between Lakshmi Durga and her husband over the relationship, following which she moved to her parents’ house.Police said Gouri Shankar allegedly conspired with his wife and her brother, Varri Narasimha, to eliminate Lakshmana. The investigation revealed that the accused had allegedly paid supari to others to execute the murder.Investigators also found that Gouri Shankar had transferred a total of Rs 1.79 lakh to various bank accounts on the instructions of his brother-in-law, Narasimha. Police are examining the transactions as part of the investigation.As part of the alleged plan, Lakshmana was called over the phone to Polasanipalli village in Bhimadolu mandal on the night of September 19. He was allegedly taken to the Dalamma–Dalappa pond, where he was served liquor and beaten to death with an iron rod, police said.The accused allegedly transported the body on a motorcycle and dumped it in the Polavaram canal near Pangidigudem bridge in an attempt to destroy evidence.The body was found in the canal near Pedavegi on September 21. Pedavegi police initially registered a case after treating it as an unidentified body. Subsequent investigation established the deceased’s identity as Thumula Lakshmana, following which the case was transferred to Bhimadolu police station.Narasimha was arrested on October 8. Dwarapureddy Ganesh and Doddani Suresh Kumar, who allegedly assisted in the murder, were also arrested, while a juvenile allegedly involved in the crime was taken into custody.With the arrests of Gouri Shankar and Lakshmi Durga on Thursday, police said the investigation into the murder had made further progress.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Vijayawada | Silver Rate in Vijayawada | Bank Holidays in Vijayawada | Public Holidays in Vijayawada | Petrol Price in Vijayawada | Diesel Price in Vijayawada | CNG Price in Vijayawada | LPG Price in VijayawadaStay updated with the latest Vijayawada news. articles.title: Cane farmers refuse to call off march despite CM’s appeal, demand sugar MSP first
articles.summary: Sugarcane farmers continue padayatra to Hirebagewadi toll despite CM DK Shivakumar’s appeal, demanding MSP for sugar and cane pricing before any panel.
articles.body: Belagavi: Sugarcane farmers Thursday refused to call off their march to Hirebagewadi toll plaza despite an appeal from chief minister DK Shivakumar and instead demanded that the Centre announce minimum support price (MSP) first and form a committee later.Hundreds of farmers reached Belagavi city in the evening after covering 35 km from Hattaragi toll plaza in Hukkeri taluk. Volunteers welcomed them with food and water. They are expected to reach Hirebagewadi Friday morning. Kannada organisations and bar association advocates have extended support.Chunappa Pujeri, state president, Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha and Hasiru Sene, revealed he had received a call from Shivakumar, who urged farmers to halt the agitation since it was inconveniencing public. “We respect the CM, but we will not call off the protest. We have left one side of the national highway open for traffic,” he said.Farmers want sugar MSP fixed at Rs 60 per kg and cane priced at Rs 5,500 per tonne, which Pujeri called justified given the retail price of sugar.“We welcome the Centre’s decision to form a committee, but we cannot wait months for its report as the crushing season is approaching,” he said. He asked why no such panels were formed before petrol, diesel and fertiliser prices were raised.Pujeri blamed Union minister Pralhad Joshi for the protests, alleging he had “deceived farmers” during talks in New Delhi. Joshi, meanwhile, has written to Shivakumar, urging the state govt to implement relief measures, including a state-advised price. He also appealed for the protest to be withdrawn.Following his meeting with farmers on Monday, Joshi constituted a committee and sought action on three issues: independent verification of sugar recovery figures, periodic calibration of weighing machines at mills, and a review of deductions on mechanically harvested cane.Deputy commissioner Mohammad Roshan and city police commissioner Prakash Nikam met farmers on the highway and urged them to stay peaceful. “The district administration has sent details on demands to the state and central govts. articles.title: Ex-minister Anbil Mahesh moves HC for anticipatory bail
articles.summary: Ex-TN minister Anbil Mahesh seeks anticipatory bail in Madras HC in ₹100 crore private school recognition scam case; CCB to file response, hearing Oct 16.
articles.body: Chennai: DMK leader and former school education minister Anbil Mahesh has approached the Madras high court seeking anticipatory bail., apprehending arrest in connection with the ₹100 crore private schools recognition cheating case.Anbil Mahesh moved the bail application after the high court refused him interim relief from police action in a plea seeking to quash the FIR registered against him in connection with the case. On Thursday, when the plea came up for hearing, Justice V Lakshminarayanan directed Chennai Central Crime Branch (CCB) police to file its response and adjourned the hearing to Oct 16.The issue pertains to a complaint alleging that more than ₹100 crore was illegally collected during the previous govt by promising to secure permanent recognition, DTCP and CMDA approvals, and other statutory clearances for more than 1,000 private schools.Based on the complaint, Chennai CCB initially registered a case against a private school’s association president P T Arasakumar and others.
